name: Bloom Energy
description: Bloom Energy builds solid-oxide fuel-cell power plants (Energy Servers) that make electricity onsite from natural gas, biogas or hydrogen without combustion, mainly for data centers and other large power users that cannot wait for the grid. Most revenue is a one-time sale of the Energy Server plus installation, with a recurring layer from long-term service contracts and a small amount from selling electricity under power purchase agreements. Revenue rose 37% to $2,024M in 2025 and it reported its first operating profit of this size ($72.8M), but the 10-K reports a net loss of $88.4M attributable to common stockholders, and three customers made up 43%, 13% and 12% of revenue.

employees.note: 2,214 full-time employees: 1,752 in the US, 395 in India and the rest elsewhere.

businessLines.name: Product
businessLines.how: Sells Energy Server fuel-cell systems to end customers, financiers and distributors, usually priced per kilowatt installed.

businessLines.name: Installation
businessLines.how: Customers pay to install the Energy Server onsite (site work, interconnection) on top of the product price.

businessLines.name: Service
businessLines.how: Annual operations and maintenance agreements keep systems running and performing over the contract life; recurring revenue.

businessLines.name: Electricity
businessLines.how: Sells electricity generated by Energy Servers it owns or operates under power purchase agreements, billed per kilowatt-hour.

brands.name: Fund JVs (with Brookfield Asset Management)
brands.note: Joint venture entities formed August 2025 under a prospective financing framework of up to $5.0 billion over five years for future Bloom projects; accounting for them is flagged as a critical audit matter. The 10-K says its largest 2025 customer (43% of revenue) is a related party.

whatsNext.text: AEP supply agreement: up to 1 GW of Bloom fuel cells, initial order 100 MW, expansion phases expected in future years (announced November 2024)

Oracle agreed to receive a warrant for 3,531,073 shares at $113.28 per share, expiring six months after issuance, in connection with a partnership for onsite power for AI data centers (warrant terms still to be negotiated per 10-K)
